jobs.title: Senior Consultant, Lead Wetland Delineator
jobs.description:
Shape the Future of Responsible Development While Protecting Critical Ecosystems

Wetlands are more than landscapes—they’re complex, living systems that safeguard water quality, biodiversity, and community resilience. As a Senior Consultant, Lead Wetland Delineator
at ERM
, based in Cleveland, Ohio,
you’ll play a strategic role in balancing environmental protection with the infrastructure and energy projects that shape our world. Your expertise will help clients make informed, environmentally sound decisions that drive sustainable progress across the Midwest and beyond.

Why This Role Matters

Your work ensures wetlands and sensitive habitats are identified, protected, and responsibly managed. Every delineation, assessment, and technical report you lead directly supports ERM’s mission to advance environmental stewardship, regulatory compliance, and sustainability for our clients and the communities they serve.

What Your Impact Is

Lead wetland delineations and protected species assessments for high‑profile, high‑impact projects.
Produce technical reports, datasets, and compliance strategies that influence infrastructure planning and regulatory outcomes.
Partner with ERM Project Managers and senior leaders to deliver innovative, fit‑for‑purpose environmental solutions.
Shape permitting pathways and impact assessments across renewable energy, utilities, land development, and other key sectors.

Required

What You’ll Bring

BS in environmental science, biology, natural resources, or a related discipline (minimum 3.0 GPA), or equivalent experience.
3+ years of experience (5 years strongly preferred) in environmental consulting or related field.

Technical Skills

Wetland delineation using the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers Wetlands Delineation Manual and Regional Supplements.
Plant identification, soil sampling, hydric soil indicators, and hydrology field assessment.
Strong data management and technical report writing capabilities.

Other Requirements

Driver's License Required: This position requires a valid driver's license and/or the ability to operate a company vehicle due to the nature of job duties, which include frequent travel to various client locations across a large geographical area.
Ability to travel up to 75%.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office.
Strong communication, analytical, and problem‑solving skills.
Ability to work independently and collaboratively in dynamic field and project environments.
This position is not eligible for immigration sponsorship.

Preferred

Professional Wetland Certificate (nationwide) and experience working in the Midwest.
Experience with NEPA environmental assessments, permitting, and compliance documentation.
Familiarity with U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, National Marine Fisheries Service, and state/local regulatory requirements.

Key Responsibilities

Perform wetland delineations across Upper Midwest states using federal and regional protocols.
Conduct habitat assessments, environmental due diligence, and NEPA‑related impact analysis.
Prepare multi‑media environmental permitting materials and compliance management plans.
Support project delivery through field surveys, data interpretation, literature reviews, and technical reporting.
Collaborate with cross‑functional teams to develop recommendations and strategic solutions for clients.
Manage quality, budgets, and timelines in alignment with ERM’s Impact Assessment team objectives.

For the Senior Consultant, Lead Wetland Delineator
position, the anticipated annual base pay is $69,386–$102,301 (USD)
. Actual pay will depend on factors such as education, experience, skills, location, performance, and business needs. In some cases, pay may fall outside this range. This role may be eligible for bonus pay (casual and fixed term/flex force employees are not bonus eligible).

We offer a comprehensive benefits package, including paid time off, parental leave, medical, dental, vision, life, disability, AD&D insurance, 401(k) or RRSP/DPSP, and other applicable benefits to eligible employees.

Note
: Bonuses, commissions, and other forms of additional compensation are not guaranteed and subject to the sole discretion of ERM and its policies and procedures.

Who We Are

As the largest global pure play sustainability consultancy, we partner with the world’s leading organizations, creating innovative solutions to sustainability challenges and unlocking commercial opportunities that meet the needs of today while preserving opportunity for future generations.

At ERM we know that creating a diverse, equitable and inclusive work environment is an essential part of making our company a great place to build a career. We also see our diversity as a strength that helps us create better solutions for our clients. Our diverse team of world-class experts supports clients across the breadth of their organizations to operationalize sustainability, underpinned by our deep technical expertise in addressing their environmental, health, safety, risk and social issues. We call this capability our “boots to boardroom” approach for its comprehensive service model that allows ERM to develop strategic and technical solutions that advance objectives on the ground or at the executive level.

Please submit your resume and brief cover letter.

ERM does not accept recruiting agency resumes. Please do not forward resumes to our jobs alias, ERM employees or any other company location. ERM is not responsible for any fees related to unsolicited resumes.

ERM is proud to be an Equal Employment Opportunity employer. We do not discriminate based upon race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, status as a protected veteran, status as an individual with a disability, or other applicable legally protected characteristics.

Thank you for your interest in ERM!

Company Description

Veolia in North America is the top-ranked environmental company in the United States for three consecutive years, and the country's largest private water operator and technology provider as well as hazardous waste and pollution treatment leader. It offers a full spectrum of water, waste, and energy management services, including water and wastewater treatment, commercial and hazardous waste collection and disposal, energy consulting and resource recovery. Veolia helps commercial, industrial, healthcare, higher education and municipality customers throughout North America. Headquartered in Boston, Veolia has more than 10,000 employees working at more than 350 locations across North America.

Job Description

Position Purpose:

This position provides specialized transportation and disposal services to our clients. Responsibilities include

manifesting, packaging, spill response, labeling, loading/unloading, coordinating transportation, and

sampling/profiling material while adhering to state and federal environmental, health, and safety regulations.

Primary Duties/Responsibilities

Sample waste streams according to prescribed policies and procedures.
Manifesting, packaging, spill clean-up response and remedial activities, labeling, loading, off loading, and coordinating transportation.
Maintain a professional image to clients by answering inquiries and suggesting solutions to existing/potential problems.
Comply and enforce all compliance, health, safety, and procedures in accordance with VES-TS policies.
Become familiar with all U. S. Department of Transportation (DOT)/Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) and VES-TS regulations required in submitting paper work to expedite disposal of hazardous waste.
Operate and maintain all equipment in a professional manner to ensure optimum efficiency and effectiveness.
Other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

Education/Experience/Background:

High School diploma or General Educational Development (GED) required
Bachelor's degree in Chemistry or related science discipline preferred

Knowledge/Skills/Abilities

Strong team player
Excellent interpersonal and communication skills
Time management: the ability to organize and manage multiple deadlines
Strong customer service orientation
Computer proficiency
Ability to follow through on assignments.

Required Certification/Licenses/Training

40-hour HAZWOPER Certification
Valid Drivers License
Ability to obtain a Class A or B Commercial Drivers License (CDL) with Hazardous (H) endorsement

NOAA's National Geodetic Survey (NGS) provides the framework for all positioning activities in the Nation. The foundational elements of latitude, longitude, elevation, and shoreline information impact a wide range of important activities. NGS is responsible for mapping the 95,000 miles of the U.S. shoreline. Currently the CMP has a data base of over half a million aerial photographs and thousands of shoreline maps.

Entarian is seeking a candidate for our LIDAR Technical / Cartographer position to support ongoing topographic/bathymetric LIDAR projects. The best candidate will understand NGS' strategic goals and its mandate for shoreline mapping under the CMP. Job duties include:

Analyze and edit topobathy point cloud LIDAR data to ensure proper classification of shoreline features and accurate representation of bathymetric depth.
Compile, edit, and attribute shoreline shapefile products to delineate mean high water and mean low water for the U.S. and its territories.
Quality assurance and quality control of contractor produced topobathy LIDAR data, normalized intensity data, topobathy DEMs, and total propagated uncertainty (TPU) data through detailed visual inspection and metadata verification.
Resolve complex discrepancies in source material by researching and cross-referencing historical charts, legacy imagery, and Electronic Navigational Chart shapefiles.
Ensure all cartographic products maintain strict compliance with NGS LIDAR, topology, and data stewardship standards.
Provide expert-level technical guidance and training to new personnel to ensure consistency in shoreline delineation and attribution.
Collaborate on the development of innovative tools and methodologies to streamline production workflows and integrate emerging geospatial technologies.

Senior Coral Reef Restoration Specialist
jobs.description:
Entarian is seeking a Senior Coral Reef Restoration Specialist to provide technical leadership and support for coral reef restoration activities for the NOAA Office of Habitat Conservation, Restoration Center. This position will support the coordination, planning, implementation, monitoring, and oversight of coral reef restoration projects, with particular emphasis on Natural Resource Damage Assessment (NRDA) restoration planning and implementation, environmental compliance, project management, and collaboration with federal, state, nonprofit, and other restoration partners. The position requires the ability to support field activities and may require periodic regional site visits and meetings with partners, with regular off-site work acceptable. The contractor may be required to travel for meetings, workshops, trainings, conferences, and field activities.

Duties Include

Coordinate coral reef restoration activities across NOAA, partner organizations, coral nursery sites, propagation programs, researchers, resource managers, nonprofit organizations, and other stakeholders to support consistent and effective restoration approaches.
Support development and implementation of coral reef restoration coordination plans, best management practices, permitting and authorization requirements, capacity building, technology and methods transfer, and resilience-based recovery strategies.
Provide technical management and oversight of trustee or responsible-party coral restoration projects, including coordination and development of restoration plans, assessment reports, environmental compliance documents, monitoring plans, permit requests, project budgets, adaptive management plans, and restoration scaling activities.
Plan, execute, and implement small- and large-scale coral restoration actions associated with NRDA cases, including emergency, primary, and compensatory restoration, and support the scaling of Natural Resource Damages to appropriate restoration.
Support NRDA restoration planning under the Oil Pollution Act (OPA) and Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Act (CERCLA), including coordination with state and federal trustees, project identification and selection, restoration concepts and designs, monitoring and evaluation plans, case strategy, and technical research.
Provide project management support for coral restoration projects, including identifying project milestones, developing and maintaining budgets and schedules, overseeing and tracking progress, coordinating contracting activities, and supporting project implementation and reporting.
Provide field oversight and technical expertise for coral restoration and monitoring activities, including site evaluation, implementation and refinement of monitoring programs, data collection and synthesis, emergency coral restoration, and support for regional coral reef monitoring activities.
Evaluate and synthesize multi-year coral restoration monitoring data, identify data gaps, conduct or support statistical analyses, refine monitoring protocols, and develop technical reports, memoranda, and scientific publications.
Develop and support environmental compliance documentation and permitting, including NEPA Environmental Assessments and documentation supporting Environmental Impact Statements; coordinate with NOAA General Counsel for Natural Resources and applicable regulatory agencies; and support consultation requirements under the Magnuson-Stevens Fishery Conservation and Management Act and Endangered Species Act.
Support fishery habitat restoration projects that benefit fisheries, protected species, and coastal resilience, including project identification, conceptual design, feasibility assessment, prioritization, implementation, monitoring, and adaptive management.
Collaborate and communicate with federal, state, nonprofit, scientific, and other partners to enhance restoration outcomes and effectively navigate complex technical and programmatic issues.
Support cross-NOAA coral restoration coordination, including communication and collaboration among NOAA programs and offices, leadership of recurring coordination meetings, development of meeting materials and notes, and dissemination of information to program leadership.
Develop restoration plans, annual reports, leadership briefings, technical reports, and other written products supporting coral reef restoration activities.
Perform data management and reporting activities, including accurate and timely tracking of project information in RCDB, DARRTS, SharePoint, and other reporting systems; maintaining Administrative Records and case websites; and coordinating information requests and process improvements.

The position is fully remote with periodic on-site meetings, regional site visits, and meetings with partners throughout the Southeast required. The contractor may also be required to travel for workshops, trainings, and conferences.

The salary for this position is approximately $74,000 - 94,000/year.

Minimum Qualifications

Master’s degree in biology, ecology, natural resource management, environmental science, marine science, or a related discipline, with 8–10 years of specialized professional experience directly related to coral reef restoration and marine resource management.
Expertise in marine habitats, specifically coral reef ecosystems and coral reef restoration.
Demonstrated experience implementing and coordinating coral reef restoration activities.
Experience providing technical oversight of coral reef restoration projects, including restoration planning, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation.
Experience with NRDA restoration planning and implementation, including restoration projects conducted under the Oil Pollution Act and/or CERCLA.
Experience planning and implementing restoration actions associated with NRDA cases and developing or supporting restoration plans, environmental compliance documents, monitoring plans, permit requests, and restoration scaling.
Experience developing and implementing monitoring plans and programs in coral reef environments.
Strong project management skills, including the ability to identify project milestones, develop and maintain budgets and schedules, oversee and track progress, and manage multiple restoration activities.
Ability to support coral reef field activities and visually identify commonly encountered coral reef-related marine organisms, including fish.
Strong understanding of coastal and offshore ecology applicable to coral reef ecosystems.
Strong collaboration skills and demonstrated ability to work effectively with federal, state, nonprofit, scientific, and other restoration partners.
Strong oral and written communication skills, including demonstrated authorship of peer-reviewed scientific literature and the ability to develop restoration plans, technical reports, annual reports, and materials for program leadership.
Understanding of federal policy and the NRDA process.
Current certification, or ability to become certified, as a NOAA Scientific Diver and/or Working Diver, as well as certification in First Aid, CPR, and Oxygen Administration.
Ability to work independently, manage competing priorities, and support occasional travel and field activities.
Must be a U.S. Citizen or Permanent Resident and be able to pass a background investigation to obtain a security badge to access applicable government systems and facilities.

Desired Qualifications

Extensive practical experience implementing and overseeing large-scale coral reef restoration projects.
Experience with NEPA environmental compliance and development of Environmental Assessments and documentation supporting Environmental Impact Statements.
Experience with ESA, MSA, and other applicable marine resource protection statutes.
Experience coordinating coral restoration activities across multiple organizations, programs, or geographic areas.
Experience with emergency coral restoration following physical impact events.
Experience synthesizing long-term coral reef monitoring datasets and developing technical or peer-reviewed scientific publications.
Experience with restoration project and case-management systems such as RCDB, DARRTS, and SharePoint.
Experience working with NOAA or another federal natural resource agency.

Entarian is seeking a Gulf Habitat Restoration Specialist to provide technical, programmatic, environmental compliance, outreach, and restoration planning support for the NOAA Office of Habitat Conservation, Restoration Center. This position will support fishery habitat restoration and related NOAA programs and initiatives in the Northern Gulf of America, with an emphasis on wetland and coastal habitat restoration, restoration planning, environmental compliance, and project management.

Duties Include

Support fishery habitat restoration planning and implementation, including the evaluation, identification, prioritization, design, implementation, and monitoring of restoration projects, with particular emphasis on habitats and biological resources of the Northern Gulf of America.
Support restoration projects involving wetlands and coastal habitats, including living shorelines, salt and tidal marshes, oyster habitat, and barrier islands, and apply ecological principles to habitat restoration planning, implementation, and monitoring.
Provide technical and programmatic support for restoration planning and DARRP cases, including coordination with NOAA staff, local partners, state and federal trustees, responsible parties, technical professionals, and other stakeholders to support project development, implementation planning, monitoring, adaptive management, and reporting.
Support project solicitation, review, and tracking activities, including distribution of requests for proposals, review and scoring of proposals, participation in technical review discussions, development of monitoring plans, participation in implementation planning, review of progress reports, and tracking of project accomplishments.
Provide technical management and oversight of trustee or responsible-party restoration projects, including coordination of draft restoration plans, assessment reports, environmental compliance documents, monitoring and evaluation plans, permit requests, project budgets, adaptive management plans, and restoration scaling activities.
Support Natural Resources Damage Assessment (NRDA) restoration planning and related activities, including gathering information from state and federal trustees, supporting case strategy and decisions through literature and expert-opinion research, preparing topic papers, and supporting the identification, selection, planning, and implementation of restoration projects.
Provide programmatic and project management support, including project scheduling, budgeting, tracking project milestones and deliverables, coordinating field activities and subcontractor oversight, and managing multiple concurrent and competing projects and responsibilities.
Develop and support environmental compliance documentation and permitting, including NEPA documentation using established NOAA and CEQ methods and guidance; Section 106 of the National Historic Preservation Act; and documentation needed to support compliance with applicable federal, state, and local requirements, including the Endangered Species Act and Magnuson-Stevens Fishery Conservation and Management Act.
Coordinate and communicate with federal, state, local, and non-governmental partners and stakeholders, including navigating competing priorities and communicating complex technical and restoration issues.
Develop outreach and communication products, including draft press releases, project fact sheets, briefing packets, maps, story maps, and other materials; and support public meetings, events, and other outreach activities as needed.
Perform data management and reporting activities, including compiling and inputting project data into the Restoration and Conservation Database (RCDB), DARRTS, and other reporting databases; coordinating information requests; and working with the IT team on potential process improvements.

Experience with Natural Resources Damage Assessment (NRDA), the Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Act (CERCLA), and the Oil Pollution Act (OPA).
Knowledge of federal, state, and local regulations related to living marine resources and habitat restoration projects.
Demonstrated ability to perform field monitoring and habitat assessment activities to identify and evaluate habitat restoration projects.
